clue.text: It's a mistake — whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: reading from either end gives the same word, so the answer reads identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone insists that an error is an error from every angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is informal British slang for a blunder or gaffe.

clue.text: Small piece in support for malicious talk

indicators.note: the small piece sits inside the word for support, so 'in' signals the container

parts.note: backing is support, as for a cause
a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A tiny scrap of encouragement is all it takes to fuel nasty gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Backbiting is spiteful talk about someone behind their back, a synonym for malicious gossip.

clue.text: From which, in the high street, there may be a song and dance?

definitions.text: From which, in the high street, there may be a song and dance?

parts.words: From which, in the high street, there may be a song and dance?
parts.note: a high-street hairdresser's shop seems meant, but the singing points to the close-harmony style named after such shops; a song and dance is also a fuss

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at where a commotion on the shopping street comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' reads as a fuss, but here it hints at barbershop quartets, the American close-harmony singing tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbershop is both a men's hairdresser on the street and a style of unaccompanied harmony singing.

clue.text: Superior involved in some chaos

indicators.note: the word for superior is wrapped up inside the word for some, so 'involved in' signals a container

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'
arch as a prefix or adjective means chief or superior, as in archbishop

explanation.surface: A boss caught up in a bit of disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is lawless disorder, a close synonym for chaos.

clue.text: Shouts loudly for camera part

definitions.meaning: to bellow is to roar or yell, so this is the verb in the third person
older folding cameras have a pleated expandable section between lens and body

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for roaring and the name of the pleated bellows on a folding camera.

clue.text: Card game not starting — there's a lot of pressure in it

definitions.text: there's a lot of pressure in it

indicators.note: the card game loses its opening letter, so 'not starting' signals removing the first letter

parts.note: bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: A card game that won't get going while everyone feels the strain.
explanation.walkthrough: In weather maps a ridge is an elongated area of high atmospheric pressure, which makes the cryptic definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorologists call an elongated zone of high barometric pressure a ridge.

clue.text: Space in our home so muddled

indicators.note: something muddled is jumbled up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: There's no room in our house because it is such a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muddled' rearranges OUR HOME SO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Houseroom means space or accommodation, as in 'I wouldn't give it houseroom'.

clue.text: Look in hold on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue the word climbs the column, so it is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to keep something is to hold it

explanation.surface: Glancing into the castle tower while climbing its stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the way up' turns KEEP backwards; 'in' is a link word, and a keep is also a castle tower, adding to the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A peek is a quick, furtive look or glance.

clue.text: Forebear? No traces, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A lament that no trace remains of a forefather.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is a forebear, a person from whom one is descended.

clue.text: Flexible body armour with circular letters?

definitions.meaning: armour of linked metal rings worn by medieval soldiers
chain letters are circulated from person to person, so their post is a playful second reading

explanation.definitionFit: Linked-ring armour is called chain mail, and post made of chain letters would jokingly be chain mail too.

clue.text: Devil of a score at Wimbledon?

definitions.meaning: the ... is an old euphemism for the devil, as in 'what the ...'
in tennis, forty-all is called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: The word serves both as a mild oath for the devil and the tennis term for a tied forty-all score.

clue.text: Move forcefully on board?

definitions.meaning: to push one's way roughly through, as in barging past
a flat-bottomed canal boat is something you would be on board

explanation.definitionFit: To barge is to shove one's way along, and a barge is also a cargo boat that people ride on.

clue.text: End with Edward's secret

parts.note: close means end, as in the close of play
Ted is a familiar short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Concluding with something Edward has kept to himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Closeted describes something kept private or hidden, so it means secret.

clue.text: Who'd remain a duke even when losing his head?

definitions.text: Who'd remain a duke even when losing his head?

parts.words: Who'd remain a duke even when losing his head?
parts.note: the victor of Waterloo was a duke, and without his first letter his title names the jazz bandleader also known as Duke

explanation.surface: A riddle about an aristocrat who survives beheading with his title intact.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first letter of the Iron Duke's title and you reach Ellington, the jazz great nicknamed Duke, so he stays a duke either way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Wellington beheaded becomes Duke Ellington, still a 'Duke'.

clue.text: Grass found in Bible book

definitions.meaning: a meadow grass grown for hay, named after an American farmer
two New Testament epistles from Paul are addressed to this disciple

explanation.definitionFit: Timothy names both a hay grass and two letters of Paul in the New Testament.

clue.text: Computer accessories or accommodation for rodents?

definitions.meaning: mats on which a computer pointing device is moved
a pad is slang for a home, so a mouse's flat would be a mouse pad

explanation.definitionFit: Mouse mats for computers share their name with a jokey idea of homes for mice.

clue.text: Guess model after drink

indicators.note: the model's word comes after the drink's word, so 'after' orders the two pieces

parts.note: to sup is to drink, in sips
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone takes a guess at the next sitter after a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose is to assume or guess without proof.

clue.text: Tick peer off, he's stopping work

indicators.note: off suggests something is wrong or out of place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Annoying a nobleman, as a worker downs tools.
explanation.definitionFit: A picketer is a striker who stands outside a workplace, having stopped work.

clue.text: Change Renault gear, perhaps

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of these letters

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Advice to shift gear in a French car.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutral is the gear position in which no drive is engaged, an example of a gear.

clue.text: Type of fringe for the nut

definitions.meaning: the extremist minority of a movement is called the ... fringe
nut is slang for a mad person

explanation.definitionFit: Lunatic qualifies the phrase for an extremist fringe group and is also a noun for a crazy person.

clue.text: Fraction claimed to be wrong

indicators.note: being wrong suggests the letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone asserts that a fraction is incorrect.
explanation.definitionFit: A decimal is a fraction written in base-ten notation after a point.

clue.text: French composer liberal in early letters

indicators.note: the liberal abbreviation goes inside the letters, so 'in' signals the container

parts.note: D's and E's, two letters early in the alphabet, spelt out as dees

explanation.surface: A French musician with progressive views shows up in his first correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early letters' is DEES, the spelt-out plural of D and E; Léo Delibes wrote the ballet Coppélia.
explanation.definitionFit: Léo Delibes was a nineteenth-century French composer of ballets and operas.

clue.text: Deathly part of Heathrow?

definitions.meaning: ... describes an illness ending in death
the London airport is divided into numbered passenger buildings

explanation.definitionFit: Terminal means fatal, and the passenger buildings at an airport are called terminals.

clue.text: A fly seen in humid Georgia

indicators.note: the answer is visible inside the run of these two words

explanation.surface: Spotting an insect in the muggy southern US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny gnat-like fly that often swarms in damp places.

clue.text: Contract long forgotten in German city

indicators.note: something forgotten is left out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: to contract is to shrink or lessen
L is the abbreviation for long, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A long-forgotten agreement found in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in Germany's Ruhr valley.

clue.text: Country health resort fashionable

parts.note: a spa is a resort with mineral springs
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: Describing a nation with a trendy wellness retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a country on the Iberian peninsula, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Auntie's a busy person with book

parts.note: a hard worker is called a busy bee

explanation.surface: An aunt is a hard worker who always carries a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie and the Beeb are both British nicknames for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC is affectionately nicknamed both 'Auntie' and 'the Beeb' in Britain.

clue.text: Dash to back of beyond for an antelope

parts.note: élan is dash or flair

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: Rushing to the back of beyond in search of a wild antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiral horns.

clue.text: Sally seen in Catholic newspaper with food additive

indicators.note: Sally's short form appears inside the newspaper's name, so 'seen in' signals a container

parts.note: The Tablet is a long-running British Catholic weekly
Sal is a pet form of Sally

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally appears in a religious paper with a food item.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tablet is a British Roman Catholic weekly paper; 'seen in' puts the pet name inside it, near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Table salt is common salt added to food for seasoning, an additive.

clue.text: Mean to include one unfinished drawing for hopeless type

indicators.note: the base word wraps around the others, so 'to include' signals a container

parts.note: base means mean or low-minded

indicators.note: the drawing loses its final letter, so an unfinished word drops its end

parts.note: a sketch is a rough drawing
A is the article meaning one

explanation.surface: A stingy person sketches incompletely, ending in despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' drops the drawing's last letter; that and the one go between the second and third letters of the base word, which 'to include' wraps round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket case is informal for someone useless or unable to cope.

clue.text: A less than positive response from the Elysee shortly

parts.words: less than positive response from the Elysee
parts.note: non is French for no, a negative reply from the French president's palace

explanation.surface: France's presidential palace gives a lukewarm answer quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Élysée Palace is the French president's residence, so its 'no' is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an archaic word for soon or shortly.
